other.about: Ageing settings (T1, T2; handoff 6.3): epoch step sizes, when detailed windows open, the predictability horizon, the ageing star's wind and the names of white dwarf colours.

processes.about: TP4 (time design sections 6, 9 and 10): every process that depends on time says its shape (line, stream or march), its own time tau as physics (a block or an Equation, never a typed number), its anchor, the marks it can publish and, for a march, its grid rule, and which kernel ops read it. The list is the pace ladder (op pace_ladder); a kernel op that takes a date and is named by no declaration fails a check (handover/packages/TP4-undeclared-ops.txt, a ledger that only shrinks). A pack may add a declaration or replace one by its id.

marks: a change of phase (subgiant, giant, white dwarf)
list.how: Drawn once when the star resolves (sse-time star.rs state_at and mass_at); any age is a read of the curve. Its own time is how long it burns hydrogen. Until TP2 the anchor is the star's age in years, read through dated's convention.

list.says: A system ageing with its star
list.grid: The star's own phases: main-sequence steps of main_sequence_step_myr, then subgiant_steps, giant_steps and white_dwarf_steps (this pack's time settings), with a window over a close pair stepped window_steps_per_orbit times per innermost orbit. Until TP5 the grid also depends on the dates asked from and to (audit 3.4), so two legs do not yet give the bits of one.
marks: a change of the star's phase
list.how: The epoch stepper (sse-time epoch.rs) on a look-ahead branch, kept only on a yes. Mass loss is slow beside the orbits, so the orbits follow the star (section 7): the march's own time is its driver's.

list.says: A body going round its host

subjects.says: the Moon round the Earth (the Moon's own mass left out, 1.2 percent)
a world 1 au from the Sun

list.how: A Kepler orbit read at any date from its own epoch, the angle formed exactly in whole seconds (TP1, Instant::angle_since).

Flares drawn from the seed in bins set by the star's own rate (sse-activity), so any window is read without the ones before it; a window holding too many gives a count and the biggest. Its pace is the dynamo's: the time the outer layer takes to turn over. The op still takes star-age seconds as a double (TP1b).

equation.name: How long the universe takes to grow by a large share at today's rate

source.text: Hogg, D. W. 1999, Distance measures in cosmology, arXiv:astro-ph/9905116

explain.curious: At today's rate of expansion, the time it would take the universe to double in size if the rate held. It sets the pace of the cosmic web: nothing on that scale changes much faster.
explain.science: The Hubble time t_H = 1/H0, the e-folding time of the scale factor at constant H. The real age differs from it by the history of H; it is a pace, not an age.

list.how: The cosmic web read at a cosmic time (sse-cosmos), from the universe's origin.

tau.marks: the campaign's own dated events: authored facts, notes, holdings, intents, rule ticks, names

list.how: Every authored event is dated in the chronicle; what is true, known or held at a date is a read of the events up to it, so any date is a read and nothing is stepped. It has no pace of its own in physics: it moves when the GM or the rules write.

sources.reimers_eta: Reimers 1975; eta near 0.5 fits the red giant branch mass loss implied by horizontal branch stars in globular clusters (McDonald and Zijlstra 2015 give 0.477)
sources.window_hill: 2 sqrt(3) mutual Hill radii: Gladman 1993's stability limit for two planets on circular orbits
sources.window_rewrite_da: above the short-period swing of osculating semi-major axes in the Solar System (Saturn about 0.4 percent across a window), so only real changes such as scattering are written back
sources.window_steps_per_orbit: fourth-order steps per innermost orbit; the integrator's own precession, about (2 pi / steps)^4 rad per orbit, stays below secular rates
sources.horizon_myr: Laskar 1989 and 1994: the inner Solar System's Lyapunov time is about 5 Myr, so individual orbits are unpredictable beyond some tens of Myr
sources.runaway_greenhouse_flux: Kopparapu et al. 2014 (ApJL 787, L29, table 1): runaway greenhouse at 1.107 times Earth's insolation for an Earth-mass planet round a Sun-like star (the 2013 paper's 1.06 was corrected there); 1.1 used as the point oceans are lost (Wolf and Toon 2015 find a stable moist state up to about 1.1)
sources.colours: blackbody colour names by effective temperature (pack data, change freely)
sources.pollution_delay_myr: Mustill et al. 2018 and Veras 2016: scattering onto white dwarfs begins within about 100 Myr of the planetary nebula and continues for Gyr
